record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: For a feedback-controlled dynamical system in which a controller uses information about the system state to choose actions, how much can the system's performance be increased for a given amount of information? Equivalently, what quantitative bounds relate the amount of system-state information used by the controller to the attainable performance increase, including measures such as power output or efficiency?

evidence.quote: The questions we have selected mainly concern the establishment of bounds to the performance and the establishment of the thermodynamics of feedback controlled systems.
the first natural main question is how much the performance can be increased with a certain amount of information

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled dynamical system consisting of: (i) a physical system with state $X_t$ evolving stochastically in time; (ii) a measurement channel that, at chosen times, produces an outcome $Y_t$ correlated with $X_t$; and (iii) a controller that selects control actions $u_t$ based on the measurement history $Y_{\le t}$, thereby modifying the subsequent evolution of $X_t$. Let a performance functional $\mathcal{P}$ be defined on trajectories of the closed-loop system; representative examples include the average extracted power $\mathcal{P} = \lim_{T\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{T}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^T \dot W_{\text{ext}}(t)\,dt\right]$ or the thermodynamic efficiency $\eta = \mathbb{E}[W_{\text{ext}}]/\mathbb{E}[Q_{\text{in}}]$. Let $\mathcal{P}_0$ denote the optimal performance achievable by any controller that uses no measurement information (open-loop). Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a scalar measure of the amount of system-state information used by the controller, such as the mutual information $I(X;Y)$ between the state and the measurement record, or the transfer entropy from $X$ to the control signal.

Problem: Determine the sharpest universal upper bound, valid for the entire class of such feedback-controlled systems (under stated regularity assumptions on dynamics, measurements, and admissible controllers), on the performance gain $\Delta\mathcal{P} := \sup_{\text{controllers}} \mathcal{P} - \mathcal{P}_0$ as an explicit increasing function of the information budget $\mathcal{I}$. In particular, exhibit a function $F$ such that $\Delta\mathcal{P} \le F(\mathcal{I})$ holds universally, and prove that $F$ is tight by constructing systems and controllers attaining (or asymptotically approaching) equality.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: generalized second-law inequalities (Sagawa–Ueda type) bound extracted work by $k_B T$ times the mutual information acquired through measurement, and Szilard-engine-style universal bounds on work extraction have been derived. Refined bounds incorporating measurement efficiency, finite-time effects, and quantum measurements have appeared, and recent (2024–2026) work establishes tighter information-thermodynamic trade-offs and precision/efficiency bounds. A single, fully general and tight bound relating arbitrary performance measures (power, efficiency) to arbitrary information measures for all feedback-controlled dynamical systems remains open.

status_evidence.title: Information Thermodynamics: Maxwell's Demon in Nonequilibrium Dynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized second law: extracted work bounded by free-energy difference plus k_B T times mutual information from measurement.
status_evidence.claim: Mutual-information-based bound on work extraction in feedback systems is established.

status_evidence.title: Quantum information engines: Bounds on performance metrics by measurement time
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on performance metrics of quantum information engines depending on measurement time and information acquired.
status_evidence.claim: Refined performance bounds continue to be derived for specific classes.

status_evidence.title: Information-thermodynamic bounds on precision in interacting quantum systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) information-thermodynamic precision bounds for interacting quantum systems.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues; no single universal tight bound across all settings.

status_evidence.title: Necessity of Feedback Control for Quantum Maxwell Demon in Finite-Time Steady Feedback Cycle
status_evidence.snippet: A generalized Clausius inequality for finite-time steady feedback cycles is derived and shown to be tighter than previous ones.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements to known bounds are still being made, indicating the general problem is not fully closed.
